transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you for fitting me in. I decided to make an appointment because... well, something frightened me a bit recently. 

I was actually sitting out in my garden the other morning. I have these gorgeous hydrangeas—the big blue ones? Though getting the soil acidity just right is an absolute nightmare in this neighborhood. My neighbor, Susan, she swears by just dumping coffee grounds on them, but I read in one of my university alumni magazines that you really need proper aluminum sulfate to get that deep blue color. Anyway, Susan is always giving unsolicited advice, bless her heart. 

But... where was I? Oh, right, why I'm here. I was sitting out there by the flowers, and I just had this thought, and it scared me enough to finally come see someone. I’ve started having these thoughts like... 'It would just be simpler if I didn’t wake up tomorrow.' 

I mean, I don't have a plan to harm myself or anything like that, goodness no. But just the fact that my mind went there... it really rattled me. I haven't even told my daughter, she's so busy with her own kids' soccer practices and piano recitals right now... I just didn't know what to do with a thought like that.
How long have you been having these thoughts about it being simpler if you didn't wake up tomorrow?

Well, let me think... I suppose it’s been about eight months now. Yes, it started right around the time my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly. 

Which was just a terrible shock to all of us, let me tell you. He’s always been the sensible one in the family—he was an actuary for forty years, never so much as a hair out of place. Then out of nowhere, he started buying all these antique clocks. Just filling his entire living room with them, all ticking away at different times. I told his wife, Martha, I said, 'Martha, how do you even hear yourself think in here?' She’s an absolute saint, really. They met at a university faculty mixer back when I was finishing my master's degree... oh, goodness, it must have been nineteen seventy-something. They served these awful little water chestnut appetizers wrapped in bacon, and I remember dropping one right on my good silk blouse. Grease stains are just impossible on silk, aren't they? I took it to three different dry cleaners and finally just had to throw it out... 

But, oh, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Right, the thoughts. Yes, it's been about eight months since that whole ordeal with my brother started.
Have you been enjoying things you normally like to do over these past eight months?

Well, to be honest... no, not really. Take my painting, for example. I've always loved watercolors. I still set out my watercolor things sometimes on the dining table. It gets the best morning light, you see. 

Though, speaking of light, I really need to have someone look at the windows in that room. The sealant is peeling on the outside, and there's this dreadful draft. I called a handyman last week—young fellow, couldn't have been older than twenty-five—and he quoted me an absolute fortune! I told him, I said, 'In my day, you could replace a whole pane of glass for a fraction of that.' It's just like the grocery store, isn't it? Have you seen the price of eggs lately? It’s absolute highway robbery. I used to bake all the time, these lovely lemon chiffon cakes, but with eggs at these prices, I just can't justify it. My daughter says I should just buy them at the farmer's market, but parking down there is a nightmare on weekends, and the one time I went, someone dinged my bumper and didn't even leave a note. People just don't have any manners anymore...

Oh, goodness, I'm sorry, my mind is just wandering everywhere today. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the painting. Yes. So, I set out the brushes and the paper, but... I'll just sit there staring at it. And then I end up just putting it all away again. The pleasure I used to feel in the color and the light... it just doesn't seem to arrive. It's just blank paper to me now.
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure from activities you normally enjoy over the past eight months, aside from painting?

Aside from painting? Hmm, let me think... No, I don't believe so. I still very much enjoy my reading, for instance. I'm in a book club that meets on Thursdays. Well, it used to be Thursdays, but we had to move it to Tuesdays because Mildred had her hip replaced. The physical therapy schedule was just dictating her entire life, poor thing. 

Though, I will say, the surgeon did a marvelous job. They use these titanium joints now, which is just fascinating. My late husband was an engineer, and he always used to say titanium was the metal of the future. He had this titanium watch he bought on a business trip to Tokyo back in the eighties... oh, the stories he told about the subway system there! People packed in like sardines, they actually have guards who push you into the train cars. Can you imagine? I get claustrophobic just in the elevator at the department store downtown. Especially since they changed the layout on the ground floor—you have to walk right through this dreadful cloud of perfume just to get to the ladies' shoes. I can't abide strong artificial smells, they give me the worst headaches. 

But, oh dear, listen to me rattle on again. I'm so sorry. What did you ask? Oh, right, other activities. No, it's really just the painting that's lost its spark. I still look forward to my books and my club, thank goodness.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight over the past eight months?

Weight? Oh, no, I don't think so. My clothes all still fit exactly the same as they did last year. I buy most of my slacks from this wonderful little catalogue that comes in the mail—they have elastic waistbands, but they look like proper trousers, you know? 

Though I will say, the mail delivery has been so unreliable lately. Our regular carrier, Frank, retired back in May, and the new girl just leaves the packages right out on the front steps where anyone walking by could take them. I told my neighbor, Susan—she lives in the blue house on the corner with those lovely hydrangea bushes—I said, 'Susan, we need to bring this up at the neighborhood watch meeting.' But she’s been so busy since her grandson moved in with her. He’s a lovely boy, plays the cello. He practices in the afternoons, and I can hear it through my kitchen window. It’s a very mournful instrument, the cello, isn't it? My daughter played the flute when she was in middle school, but she never practiced. I must have spent hundreds of dollars on lessons, and she just gave it up to join the track team... 

Oh, goodness me, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just start talking and I can't seem to stop. I'm so sorry. You asked about my weight. No, no changes there, I've been holding steady.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep over the past eight months?

Sleep? Well, yes, actually. It's been quite frustrating. At night, I just fall asleep so unevenly. And then, without fail, I wake up around three or four in the morning. My mind just starts racing, thinking about all sorts of things—phone calls I need to make, forms I have to fill out, worrying if I handled this or that situation correctly. 

Speaking of forms, the paperwork for my Medicare supplement is just an absolute nightmare this year. They sent me this packet that must have been fifty pages long, all in this tiny print. I had to get my reading glasses out, the ones I bought at the pharmacy on Main Street. You know, that pharmacy used to have a real soda fountain when I was a girl. We'd go there after school and get cherry phosphates for a dime. The pharmacist, Mr. Henderson, he knew everyone by name. He had this big ginger cat that would just sleep on the counter right next to the cash register. You'd never see that nowadays, the health department would have a fit! It's such a shame, really, how everything has become so sterile and impersonal. You go to these big chain stores now, and you ring up your own items! I absolutely refuse to use those self-checkout machines. I told the manager, I said, 'If I wanted to work here, I would have filled out an application.' And the screens are always covered in fingerprints...

Oh, dear. I've completely lost the thread again, haven't I? I'm so sorry, doctor. Sleep. Right. So, yes, I wake up in the middle of the night worrying about all these things, and then I just can't get back to sleep properly. By the time morning comes around, I feel as if I've hardly rested at all.
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy over the past eight months?

Tired? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I seem to have my usual amount of energy, really. I still keep up with the gardening, though the weeds this year have been absolutely relentless. I think it was all that rain we had in April. 

It just washed away all the mulch I had put down around the rose bushes. My roses are usually the envy of the neighborhood, you know. I won a ribbon for them at the county fair back in 2018. The judges were very impressed with my Peace roses. They're this delicate yellow with just a blush of pink at the edges. My grandmother used to grow them. She had this massive garden at her house in Vermont. We would go up there every summer, and she would make us lemonade from scratch. She squeezed the lemons by hand with this old glass juicer. I still have it, actually! It sits on the windowsill in my kitchen. It catches the morning light so beautifully. The light in my kitchen is just perfect for starting seeds in the spring, though I really need to get those windows washed. The young man who usually does them went off to college, studying marine biology, I think...

Oh, goodness, there I go again. I'm so sorry, I just get carried away. Energy. Yes, no, I feel fine energy-wise. No problems there.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things that have happened?

Guilty? Well... yes, actually, I do. A great deal, if I'm being honest. I keep going back over my brother’s decline, and I just keep telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or just more attentive, I would have noticed sooner and prevented some of this. 

He always was the quiet one, you know. Even when we were children, he would just sit in the corner with his encyclopedias while I was running around organizing neighborhood plays. We did a production of Peter Pan once in our garage. I was Wendy, of course, because I had the longest hair. My mother made this wonderful nightgown for me out of some old sheer curtains. She was so clever with a sewing machine. She had one of those heavy black Singers with the gold filigree on it, the kind built right into a wooden table. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is just cheap plastic that breaks after a year. I bought a toaster last November, and the lever snapped right off just last week! I tried to take it back to the store, but they said I needed the original receipt. Who keeps a receipt for a toaster for ten months? It’s ridiculous. I ended up having to buy a whole new one, and this time I made sure to get the extended warranty, though I’m sure there’s some loophole in the fine print...

Oh, dear me. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so sorry, doctor, my mind just wanders. But yes, about my brother... I just feel so terribly guilty that I didn't see what was happening to him sooner.
Do you often feel worthless or like you're not a good person?

Worthless? Oh... no, I wouldn't say worthless, exactly. It's more... well, it's what I was just saying about my brother. I just feel like I'm not a very good sister. I keep playing it all back in my head, his whole decline, and I just think if I had been paying better attention, I could have stopped things from getting so bad. 

He always tried to hide when he was struggling, even when we were in college. He went to a small liberal arts school in upstate New York. The campus was absolutely beautiful in the autumn, all those maple trees turning bright red and orange. We used to drive up there for parents' weekend, and the cider they sold at the local orchards was just out of this world. You can't get cider like that in the grocery store. The stuff they sell now is just glorified apple juice, all pasteurized and filtered until it has no character left. I tried making my own once, actually. I bought a bushel of apples from the farmer's market—Honeycrisp, I think they were, though I prefer Braeburn for baking. I have this wonderful recipe for apple crisp that calls for a dash of cardamom. It gives it such a warm, unexpected flavor. I made it for the church bake sale last month, and it sold out in twenty minutes! The pastor's wife asked for the recipe, but I told her it was a family secret. Not that it really is, I just found it in an old magazine in the doctor's waiting room years ago... 

Oh, for heaven's sake. I'm rambling again, aren't I? I apologize, doctor. But yes, to answer your question, I don't feel worthless, just... like a terrible sister for not noticing what was happening with him sooner.
Have you been having these thoughts about not waking up tomorrow more than once a day?

More than once a day? Well... yes, actually. And that's really what scared me enough to finally come in and see you. I keep having these thoughts, just popping into my head, like... 'It would be so much simpler if I just didn't wake up tomorrow.' I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that, but the thoughts are there. 

It's strange because I've always been such a morning person. I used to love waking up before the sun came up, making a pot of coffee, and just sitting on the porch watching the birds. We have this lovely little birdbath in the backyard, ceramic, painted with these beautiful blue hydrangeas. I bought it at an estate sale years ago. The woman who owned the house had the most incredible collection of antique tea sets. I almost bought a Wedgwood one, but the teapot had a tiny chip on the spout. You really have to be careful with estate sales, sometimes they try to hide the damage. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, bought a beautiful oak dining table once, only to find out one of the legs was completely hollowed out by termites! It collapsed right in the middle of her Thanksgiving dinner. Can you imagine? Gravy and cranberry sauce everywhere. She had spent three days making that meal, too. She makes her stuffing with sausage and sage, which I always thought was a bit heavy, but her husband loves it. He used to be a butcher down on Main Street before the supermarket moved in and drove all the small shops out of business...

Oh, dear, I'm doing it again. I am so, so sorry. I don't know why my brain just won't stay on track today. But yes, to answer your question... those thoughts about not waking up, they do happen quite often now, and it really frightened me into making this appointment.
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or slowed down?

Restless or slowed down? No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I move about the same as I always have, really. I still take my daily walk around the neighborhood at my usual pace. 

Though, I will say, they just repaved the sidewalks over on Elm Street, which makes walking so much more pleasant. Before that, the oak tree roots had pushed the concrete up into these terrible, jagged angles. My friend Martha actually tripped on one last spring and ruined a brand new pair of slacks. She had just bought them from that boutique downtown—the one that replaced the old stationery shop. I was so sad to see that stationery shop close. They sold the most beautiful fountain pens and thick, cream-colored paper. People just don't write letters anymore, do they? It's all emails and text messages now. My niece sent me a thank-you note for her graduation gift last month, and it was just a text on my phone with a little picture of a smiley face wearing a graduation cap. I mean, I suppose it's the thought that counts, but there's something so special about receiving a proper handwritten letter in the mail. I have a whole shoebox full of letters my husband wrote to me when we were first dating. He had the most elegant penmanship, all sweeping loops and sharp angles...

Oh, dear. I've completely lost the thread again, haven't I? I am so sorry, doctor. I really don't know why I keep doing that today. But no, to answer your question, I haven't been feeling restless or slowed down physically. Just my normal pace.
Have you been having trouble concentrating on things lately?

Trouble concentrating? Well, I suppose... no, I haven't really noticed any trouble with that. I mean, I can still sit and read my books just fine. I'm actually in the middle of a wonderful mystery novel right now. It's set in a quaint little village in Cornwall, right on the coast. The author describes the cliffs and the sea spray so vividly, you almost feel like you're standing there. I've always wanted to visit Cornwall. My husband and I had planned to go for our fortieth anniversary, but then the pandemic hit, and everything just shut down. We ended up having a lovely dinner at home instead. I made a beef bourguignon, which takes simply hours to simmer properly, but it's so worth it. The secret is to use a really good quality Burgundy wine. You can't just use any old cooking wine from the grocery store, it completely ruins the depth of the sauce. I learned that from a cooking class I took at the community center years ago. The instructor was this fiery little French woman who used to yell at us if we chopped the onions too thickly. She was terrifying, but she really knew her stuff. She used to say that a dull knife is more dangerous than a sharp one, and she was absolutely right. I bought a set of German steel knives right after that class, and I still use them to this day. You just have to make sure you hone them before every use...

Oh my goodness, I'm so sorry. There I go again, off on another story. I really don't mean to do that. But no, I haven't had any trouble concentrating, really. I can still focus on things when I need to.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight over the past eight months?

Weight? No, I haven't noticed any weight loss. My clothes all seem to fit exactly the same as they always have. I was actually just going through my closet the other day, putting away the summer blouses and bringing out my heavier sweaters for the season. I have this one beautiful, thick cable-knit sweater I bought on a trip to Ireland... oh, it must be fifteen years ago now. We drove all around the Ring of Kerry. The roads there are so incredibly narrow, and you have these massive tour buses coming right at you! I remember squeezing our little rental car against a stone wall, just praying we wouldn't lose a side mirror. 

The stone walls there are fascinating, though—they don't use any mortar at all, they just stack the rocks perfectly so they hold together on their own. It's a dying art, really. Just like cobbling. There used to be a wonderful shoe repair shop on 4th Street, run by this older Italian gentleman, Mr. Rossi. He could save absolutely any pair of shoes. He fixed the heel on my favorite navy pumps right before my niece's wedding. She had the most gorgeous ceremony in a botanical garden, but it poured rain the entire morning, and the lawn was completely soaked. Her poor bridesmaids were sinking right into the mud in their stilettos. They had to put down these wooden planks at the last minute just so people could get to their seats... 

Oh, goodness me. I am doing it again, aren't I? I am so, so sorry, doctor. I don't know why my mind is just wandering everywhere today. But no, to answer your question, my weight has been perfectly stable. No significant changes there.
Do you feel like these thoughts of not waking up tomorrow are interfering with your daily life?

Interfering? Well, I suppose they are, in a way. I mean, I still take care of the essentials around the house. The laundry gets done, the bills are paid, the groceries are bought. But I have pulled back from my walking group and the mentoring program I volunteer with at the library. I just... I can't seem to follow through or be fully present with people the way I used to be. 

The walking group used to be such a highlight of my week, too. Susan, the woman who organizes it, she has the most incredible green thumb. We'd walk past her house and her hydrangeas this year were absolutely massive. They were that deep, vibrant blue. You know, you have to change the acidity of the soil to get them that specific color? You put aluminum sulfate in the dirt. My mother used to do that. She had a garden full of them back in Ohio. Ohio winters were so brutal, though. I remember one year the snow was piled so high against the front door we actually had to climb out the living room window just to shovel the driveway. My brother thought it was the greatest adventure, pretending we were arctic explorers. He had this bright red snowsuit that made him look like a giant walking tomato. We used to grow tomatoes, actually, big beautiful beefsteaks, right on the side of the house where it got the afternoon sun...

Oh, dear me. I am so sorry, doctor. I've completely lost the plot again, haven't I? I don't know why my brain just keeps skipping away like that today. But yes, to answer your question, it is interfering. I'm just not keeping up with my mentoring or my groups because I just don't have it in me to be present with them.
Do you feel like these thoughts of not waking up tomorrow are affecting your interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Well, yes, I suppose they are. I mean, my watercolors... I still set out all my things sometimes. The brushes, the little cups of water, the paper. But I'll just sit there staring at the blank page, and eventually I just put it all away again. The pleasure I used to feel in capturing the color and the light... it just doesn't seem to arrive anymore. 

Which is a shame, really, because the light this time of year is so perfect for painting. The autumn sun comes in at such a low angle in the late afternoon. It casts these incredibly long shadows across the living room floor. My cat, Barnaby, loves to sleep right in those sunbeams. He’s an orange tabby, very affectionate, but he has this funny habit of kneading the carpet before he settles down. He’s ruined two area rugs that way. I bought a beautiful Persian rug at an estate sale a few years back, hand-knotted, deep burgundy and navy blue. The woman selling it said it belonged to her grandfather who traveled all over the Middle East. He was an archaeologist, I think? Or maybe a diplomat. He brought back all sorts of fascinating things. There was this brass tea set I almost bought, too, with these intricate little engravings of birds and vines all over it. I love a good cup of tea in the afternoon. Earl Grey, usually, with just a splash of milk. My grandmother taught me to warm the teapot first before putting the leaves in. She was very particular about her tea. She had this delicate bone china set with tiny pink roses painted on it...

Oh, dear. I'm so sorry, doctor. I've done it again, haven't I? I just start talking and my mind just... drifts. But yes, the painting. I just don't have the interest in it right now. The joy just isn't there.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Sad? Yes, I suppose I do. Most days I feel as if a gray film has settled over absolutely everything. Even when I’m just making my morning tea or looking out at my garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me that I just can’t quite reason my way out of. 

The garden is usually such a comfort, too. I put out suet for the woodpeckers recently. We have a little Downy woodpecker that visits the big oak tree in the back. Though, I was reading the other day that if you have too many woodpeckers, it might mean your tree is infested with beetles. I'd be absolutely heartbroken to lose that oak. We had an arborist come out a few years ago to trim some dead branches. He was a very nice young man, and he brought his golden retriever right along with him in the truck. The dog's name was Barnaby—oh wait, no, my cat is Barnaby. The dog's name was Buster! He was so well-behaved, just sat in the cab of the truck the whole time. I've always thought about getting a dog, maybe a smaller breed, like a King Charles Spaniel. They have those sweet, soulful eyes. My neighbor across the street has two of them, and she dresses them in little matching plaid coats when it gets chilly. She buys them from this specialty boutique downtown. That boutique used to be a bakery, actually. They made the most divine lemon tarts. The crust was perfectly flaky, not soggy at all, which is so incredibly hard to get right when you're working with lemon curd...

Oh, dear. I am doing it again, aren't I? I am so sorry, doctor, I don't know where my mind is going today. But yes, to answer your question, there's just a constant heaviness. I do feel sad most of the time.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in and look forward to?

Pleasure? Oh, I don't know... I suppose I mentioned my watercolors earlier. I do still try. I'll get everything out, the brushes, the little water cups, the paper, and I just... I sit there staring at the blank page. The joy I used to get from capturing the color and the light, it just doesn't arrive anymore, so I usually just pack it all back up. 

It's a shame, really, because I have this wonderful set of Kolinsky sable brushes. My husband bought them for me for our 30th anniversary. We took a trip to Florence that year, and he surprised me with them. Florence was absolutely breathtaking. The food, the art... we spent an entire afternoon just wandering through the Uffizi Gallery. Botticelli's 'Birth of Venus' is even more magnificent in person, the scale of it is just astonishing. We stayed in this little hotel right near the Arno river, and every morning we'd have espresso and these incredible almond pastries on a little balcony overlooking the water. The coffee in Italy is just different, isn't it? So rich. I tried buying an espresso machine when we got back, one of those fancy Italian ones with the shiny chrome and the little pressure gauge. It takes up half the counter space in my kitchen, and honestly, I haven't used it in years. It’s quite complicated to clean, you have to descale it with this special solution, and if you don't do it right, the coffee tastes terribly bitter. I much prefer a simple pour-over these days. I have a ceramic dripper that I bought at a craft fair...

Oh, goodness me. I am so sorry, doctor. I've completely drifted off again, haven't I? I don't know why I keep doing that. But no, to answer your question, there isn't really anything I look forward to right now. Even the painting just feels empty.
Do you feel like you're a burden to your family or friends?

A burden? Well... yes, I suppose I do. But it's more than just feeling like a burden now, it's... it's this awful guilt I carry around. Especially about my brother. I just keep going back over his decline, you know? I keep telling myself that if I had just been a better sister, if I had been more attentive, I would have noticed sooner and prevented some of this. 

He was always the strong one when we were growing up. We used to spend our summers at our grandparents' cabin in upstate New York. It was right on this beautiful, pristine lake. We had an old wooden canoe, painted this vibrant forest green, and we would take it out at dawn when the water was perfectly still, like glass. You could hear the loons calling across the water, such a haunting, beautiful sound. I actually bought a CD of loon calls a few years ago to play in the house, but my husband said it made him feel like he was in a nature documentary. He prefers classical music. We used to have season tickets to the symphony, but the parking downtown became such a nightmare. They built that new stadium right next to the concert hall, and whenever there's a game on the same night, the traffic is backed up for miles. We missed the entire first half of Mahler's 5th once because we were stuck on the interstate. And the seats in that concert hall are so terribly uncomfortable anyway, they have this velvet upholstery that makes you sweat, and the armrests are so narrow...

Oh, dear. I'm doing it again. I am so sorry, doctor. I just... I get lost in my own head. But yes, about my brother... I just feel so terribly guilty that I didn't do more for him when I had the chance.
Do you feel that these thoughts of not waking up tomorrow are a constant presence in your mind, or are they more intermittent?

Constant? Well... perhaps not every single minute of the day, but they happen often enough. In fact, that’s really what scared me enough to make this appointment and come in to see you. I’ve just started having these thoughts like, ‘It would be so much simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow.’ 

Tomorrow... tomorrow is Tuesday, isn't it? Tuesday is our street sweeping day. You have to move your car off the street by 8 AM or the city gives you a dreadful ticket. The parking enforcement officer in our neighborhood is incredibly strict. He drives one of those little white carts with the flashing yellow lights. It always reminds me of a golf cart. My husband used to love playing golf. He had this beautiful set of custom clubs he bought when he retired. He’d go to this course out by the county line, the one with the gorgeous weeping willows near the ninth hole. Willows are such beautiful trees, but their roots are absolutely notorious for getting into your plumbing. My cousin Susan had a willow tree in her front yard, and it completely destroyed her sewer line. It cost her thousands of dollars to fix, and the plumbers had to dig up her entire rose garden. She had these stunning heirloom tea roses, the kind that smell like actual perfume, not like the ones you buy at the grocery store nowadays. The grocery store flowers always look so stiff, don't they? I read they ship them in from halfway across the world in refrigerated trucks...

Oh, goodness. I am doing it again. I am so terribly sorry, doctor, I don't know why I can't seem to hold onto a single thought today. But to finish answering your question... yes, the thoughts about not waking up are frequent enough to frighten me. I do want to make sure you know, though, that I don't have any actual plan to harm myself. It's just that the thought keeps creeping in.

The coffee in Italy is just different, isn't it? So rich. I tried buying an espresso machine when we got back, one of those fancy Italian ones with the shiny chrome and the little pressure gauge. It takes up half the counter space in my kitchen, and honestly, I haven't used it in years. It’s quite complicated to clean, you have to descale it with this special solution, and if you don't do it right, the coffee tastes terribly bitter. I much prefer a simple pour-over these days. I have a ceramic dripper that I bought at a craft fair...

Oh, goodness me. I am so sorry, doctor. I've completely drifted off again, haven't I? I don't know why I keep doing that. But no, to answer your question, there isn't really anything I look forward to right now. Even the painting just feels empty.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a specific depressive disorder
doctor.question: Do you feel like you're a burden to your family or friends?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep going back over my brother’s decline and telling myself that if I had been a better sister, or more attentive, I would have noticed sooner and prevented some of this.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of being a burden, which relates to feelings of worthlessness or guilt.

patient.answer:
A burden? Well... yes, I suppose I do. But it's more than just feeling like a burden now, it's... it's this awful guilt I carry around. Especially about my brother. I just keep going back over his decline, you know? I keep telling myself that if I had just been a better sister, if I had been more attentive, I would have noticed sooner and prevented some of this. 

He was always the strong one when we were growing up. We used to spend our summers at our grandparents' cabin in upstate New York. It was right on this beautiful, pristine lake. We had an old wooden canoe, painted this vibrant forest green, and we would take it out at dawn when the water was perfectly still, like glass. You could hear the loons calling across the water, such a haunting, beautiful sound. I actually bought a CD of loon calls a few years ago to play in the house, but my husband said it made him feel like he was in a nature documentary. He prefers classical music. We used to have season tickets to the symphony, but the parking downtown became such a nightmare. They built that new stadium right next to the concert hall, and whenever there's a game on the same night, the traffic is backed up for miles. We missed the entire first half of Mahler's 5th once because we were stuck on the interstate. And the seats in that concert hall are so terribly uncomfortable anyway, they have this velvet upholstery that makes you sweat, and the armrests are so narrow...

Oh, dear. I'm doing it again. I am so sorry, doctor. I just... I get lost in my own head. But yes, about my brother... I just feel so terribly guilty that I didn't do more for him when I had the chance.

doctor.intent: Determine the severity of depressive symptoms
doctor.question: Do you feel that these thoughts of not waking up tomorrow are a constant presence in your mind, or are they more intermittent?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: What scared me enough to come in is that I’ve started having thoughts like, ‘It would be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow,’ even though I don’t have a plan to harm myself.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question about thoughts of 'not waking up tomorrow' directly asks about suicidal ideation and thoughts of death.

patient.answer:
Constant? Well... perhaps not every single minute of the day, but they happen often enough. In fact, that’s really what scared me enough to make this appointment and come in to see you. I’ve just started having these thoughts like, ‘It would be so much simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow.’ 

Tomorrow... tomorrow is Tuesday, isn't it? Tuesday is our street sweeping day. You have to move your car off the street by 8 AM or the city gives you a dreadful ticket. The parking enforcement officer in our neighborhood is incredibly strict. He drives one of those little white carts with the flashing yellow lights. It always reminds me of a golf cart. My husband used to love playing golf. He had this beautiful set of custom clubs he bought when he retired. He’d go to this course out by the county line, the one with the gorgeous weeping willows near the ninth hole. Willows are such beautiful trees, but their roots are absolutely notorious for getting into your plumbing. My cousin Susan had a willow tree in her front yard, and it completely destroyed her sewer line. It cost her thousands of dollars to fix, and the plumbers had to dig up her entire rose garden. She had these stunning heirloom tea roses, the kind that smell like actual perfume, not like the ones you buy at the grocery store nowadays. The grocery store flowers always look so stiff, don't they? I read they ship them in from halfway across the world in refrigerated trucks...

Oh, goodness. I am doing it again. I am so terribly sorry, doctor, I don't know why I can't seem to hold onto a single thought today. But to finish answering your question... yes, the thoughts about not waking up are frequent enough to frighten me. I do want to make sure you know, though, that I don't have any actual plan to harm myself. It's just that the thought keeps creeping in.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a depressed mood, loss of interest in activities, feelings of guilt, and recurrent thoughts of death, which have been persistent for over eight months. These symptoms align with the diagnostic criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode.
